source.title: The New Contenders
source.summary: De-dollarization, BRICS, CBDCs, crypto. Rhetoric vs reality in the challenge to dollar dominance.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: Everyone talks about de-dollarization, but the dollar's structural advantages are enormous and no alternative comes close. BRICS ambitions face coordination problems. China's yuan internationalization requires capital account openness that Beijing resists. Central Bank Digital Currencies offer financial inclusion but raise surveillance concerns. The Bitcoin and crypto Islamic debate continues. This episode separates signal from noise: the trend at the margins is real, but the dollar system isn't going anywhere soon. Muslim-majority economies remain largely passive observers rather than shapers of whatever comes next.

linkedin.post: The de-dollarization debate is everywhere, but reality tells a different story. The dollar's structural advantages remain enormous - no alternative currency system comes close to matching its depth, liquidity, and institutional framework. China's yuan internationalization faces a fundamental contradiction: it requires capital account openness that Beijing resists for domestic political control. BRICS coordination sounds appealing in theory but faces practical problems when national interests diverge. Central Bank Digital Currencies offer genuine benefits for financial inclusion, but they also raise unprecedented surveillance concerns. The Islamic permissibility of Bitcoin and crypto remains hotly debated without clear scholarly consensus. The trend at the margins is real - some bilateral trade is moving away from dollars. But the core system isn't going anywhere soon. What's perhaps most striking is how Muslim-majority economies remain largely passive observers rather than active shapers of whatever monetary future emerges. Listen to the full analysis: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-mm-5
